$schema_note: Maps release artifacts to their Nexus Mods targets. To publish, create a GitHub Release tagged '<artifact>-v<version>' (e.g. mapwaypointbugfixes-v1.0.0). The release.yml workflow parses the tag, stages contentDir into installDir, zips it as '<fileBaseName>_v<version>.zip' (so 'r6/...' sits at the zip root), attaches the zip to the release, and uploads to Nexus via Nexus-Mods/upload-action (beta.8, v3 upload API). See the portfolio's RELEASING notes / the nexus-ci-release-pipeline wiki page.
$paths_note: contentDir = repo folder whose CONTENTS ship. installDir = path inside the zip those contents are placed at (the in-game install path under the Cyberpunk 2077 root). fileBaseName = the download filename stem (version is appended). Pure redscript - loose .reds files under r6/scripts/MapWaypointBugFixes, no WolvenKit packing.
$contentdir_note: contentDir is 'r6' so the zip root is 'r6/scripts/MapWaypointBugFixes/*.reds'. The mod ships nothing outside r6/scripts.
$file_id_note: The Nexus file id is NOT stored here. It lives in a REPOSITORY VARIABLE named NEXUS_FILE_ID_MAPWAYPOINTBUGFIXES (uppercased, '-' -> '_'), set under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables. A file_id DOES NOT EXIST until the mod's first file has been uploaded to Nexus BY HAND, so committing a placeholder commits a lie. Get it from the mod page's Files tab > 'API Info' (Nexus labels it 'Group ID'). DO NOT use the file_id from the public v1 API -- that is a different id space and the wrong value looks entirely plausible.
